summary: dedupe_library has NO role gate at registration or handler; reachable + mutating by musician AND member roles (every other admin hygiene tool is correctly gated)
repro: POST /api/mcp tools/call dedupe_library {dryRun:true|false} as a test_account bearer with role=musician (or member). Response: 200 ok with {scanned, groupsFound, duplicatesMarked, songsMirrored, groups[]} — same shape as admin. Compare to backfill_library_index / reconcile_library / sweep_orphan_test_data which return 403 forbidden_role for the same caller.
observed: musician + member both receive successful response; can mark library_index/{id}.status='duplicate' on loser rows and mirror status into songs/{id}; default search_library + list_library hide duplicate rows so this is data-poisoning the catalog. dryRun defaults to false.
expected: 403 forbidden_role with requiredRoles:['admin'] — matching the rest of the admin hygiene tool family.

summary: Audit view does not compute parent-revocation cascade — children of a revoked root continue to report status:'active' until individually TTL-expired or revoked. Confirms C8I1-001 still present at deployed SHA db208948f.
repro: Mint a root admin bearer; mint a child from it via mint_admin_bearer; revoke the root; call list_minted_bearers — child still shows status:'active'. Could not run end-to-end this sweep (mint_admin_bearer hit 10/day quota; see C9I5-007) but the audit shape proves the gap structurally: there is no cascadeRevoked / effectiveStatus field computed against the parent.
observed: `status` field is computed solely from the child's own revokedAt + ttlExpiresAt. No parent-status awareness in the audit view.
expected: Either an explicit cascadeRevoked / effectiveStatus field on each row, OR the existing status field rendered as 'revoked' when the parent is revoked.

surface: MCP tools: list_test_accounts, cleanup_all_test_data, create_test_account, revoke_test_account
summary: Four test-tokens tools emit bare 'forbidden' as machine_code instead of the standard 'forbidden_role' rich envelope. C8I2-006 follow-up confirms still unfixed.
repro: POST /api/mcp tools/call list_test_accounts {} as musician — response machine_code='forbidden'. Compare against ~15 other tools (list_minted_bearers, mint_admin_bearer, get_ai_config, set_ai_threshold, update_setlist, etc.) which return 'forbidden_role'.
observed: `{ok:false, error:'forbidden', message:'<tool> requires admin or band_leader role.'}` — handcrafted shape, missing callerRole / requiredRoles / hint.
expected: Use forbiddenRoleEnvelope() from src/lib/mcp/error-envelopes.ts:360 so callers can pattern-match a single machine_code and get callerRole + requiredRoles + hint.

summary: PARENT §4 phrases the chart-access policy as 'charts fetchable by anyone with a fileId'. storage.rules `match /library/{allPaths=**}` is `isMember()`-gated (signed-in with role∈[member,musician,band_leader,admin]). Empirically: an unauthenticated requester CANNOT fetch chart bytes from Firebase Storage directly. Charts ARE fetchable by any signed-in role via MCP `download_chart` (server-side Admin SDK).
repro: Unauth curl against firebasestorage.googleapis.com `library/<fileId>` paths — all return 4xx. MCP download_chart with a member bearer — returns 200 + contentBase64.
observed: Storage rules are tighter than the policy phrasing suggests. No security gap — defense-in-depth.
expected: Either: (a) clarify the policy to read 'anyone in the band with a fileId' (any signed-in role), or (b) add a literally public proxy route if 'anyone' is the intent. Current state is internally consistent but the docs phrasing invites misinterpretation by future auditors (and possibly false-flag findings).

summary: 10/day mint cap is uid-scoped, not bearer-scoped. Five sibling cycle-9 sweep instances + concurrent coder lanes (cycle-8-fixes, cycle-9-hardening A/B) all share Daniel's uid 93Xn3DbS0bSNb8zmfzLyfOMX1A13 and therefore the same 10 mints. Sweep-day quota was already exhausted by mid-afternoon, blocking my admin curl row.
repro: Call mint_admin_bearer from any active sibling instance — 429 rate_limited until 2026-05-20T00:00Z. Confirmed rich envelope: {ok:false, error:{code:429, machine_code:'rate_limited'}, mintsToday:10, resetAtUtc, hint}. This closes the C8I1-002 prod-probe gap (the 429 shape was previously asserted in tests but never observed at deployed surface).
observed: Rich 429 envelope correctly populated; closes C8I1-002.
expected: Either lift the per-uid cap, add a sweep-day bypass (analogous to `[[feedback_admin_rate_limit_bypass]]` trusted-leader bypass), or have instances mint test bearers instead (works fine — what I did).

summary: PARENT §4 by-design public surfaces behave as intended. Setlists+tracks publicly readable at Firestore-rules level; /perform/setlist/<id> returns 200 HTML unauthenticated. mcpTokens/mcpOAuthClients/mcpOAuthCodes/mcpTestUsers all server-only. Deny-all fallback present.
repro: curl https://www.centralreform.live/perform/setlist/NWPBba50fltX6pNcyOVK unauthenticated → 200 text/html. Source-grep firestore.rules → mcpTokens block `allow read,write: if false;` at line 410.
observed: All by-design boundaries confirmed; no NON-chart NON-setlist private surface leaks to unauth probes.

surface: MCP framework: Zod validation vs role gate ordering
summary: Zod validation runs BEFORE the role gate on every tool I tested with invalid args (update_setlist, delete_setlist, cleanup_all_test_data, assign_musician, respond_to_assignment, set_bus_fader, set_ai_threshold, recompute_setlist_track_count). Surfaces as `result.isError:true` + nested {ok:false, error:{code:400, machine_code:'validation_error'}}. Once args are schema-valid, role gate fires correctly.
repro: Call any of the listed tools as musician with intentionally wrong arg shape → isError validation_error. Call with correct arg shape → forbidden_role 403.
observed: Per `[[feedback_mcp_validation_shape]]`. Schemas are public via tools/list anyway so no marginal info leak; the only practical downside is role-matrix auditing has to know to use schema-correct args before classifying the gate behavior.
expected: As observed — this is the documented pattern.

observed: removed:3, failures:[], aggregate:{setlists:1, mcpTokens:3, ...}; c9i1+c9i4 fixtures still present after my sweep.
